result.topic: PAN-OS XML API async log-retrieval flow (type=log) — job-id xpath, poll pending/complete shape, log-entry xpath — and whether a dedicated DNS Security log-type/filter exists

confirmedFacts.claim: Job-submission response places the job ID at xpath result/job — e.g. <response status="success" code="19"><result><msg><line>query job enqueued with jobid 18</line></msg><job>18</job></result></response>. This is byte-for-byte what the current code's _xml_log_submit already assumes.
confirmedFacts.evidence: <response status="success" code="19"><result><msg><line>query job enqueued with jobid 18</line></msg><job>18</job></result></response>

confirmedFacts.claim: pan-python's XapiClient.log() (the community/de-facto reference SDK, written by an ex-PANW engineer) independently reads the job id from the identical xpath result/job.
confirmedFacts.evidence: line 1133: job = self.element_root.find('./result/job')  /  line 1134-1135: if job is None: raise PanXapiError('no job element in type=log response')

confirmedFacts.claim: Official docs state in prose that the <log> node is ABSENT while a submitted log job is still pending, and becomes present once the job finishes — this is the only documented signal for pending-vs-complete shown with a worked example (no raw XML for the pending state itself is shown anywhere in official docs).
confirmedFacts.evidence: "When the job status is FIN (finished), the response automatically includes all the logs in the XML data response. The <log> node in XML is not present when the job status is still pending. After successful log data retrieval, the system automatically deletes the job."

confirmedFacts.claim: The reference SDK (pan-python) does NOT rely on <log>-node presence/absence at all. Its actual completion check is: poll type=log&action=get&job-id=<id>, then find('./result/job/status') and loop until status.text == 'FIN'. This is a stricter, more diagnostic mechanic than the current code's 'is <log> present' heuristic — it can distinguish 'still running' from 'finished' explicitly rather than inferring from a missing element, and it would surface a clear error via the 'no status element' exception path if the response shape ever deviates.
confirmedFacts.evidence: lines 1154-1159: status = self.element_root.find('./result/job/status') ... if status is None: raise PanXapiError('no status element in type=log&action=get response') / if status.text == 'FIN': return

confirmedFacts.claim: The completed-job response's nested log-entry xpath is result/log/logs/entry — verbatim official example: <result><job>...</job><log><logs count="20" progress="100"><entry logid="5753304543500710425"><domain>1</domain><receive_time>...</receive_time>...</entry>
confirmedFacts.evidence: <log> <logs count="20" progress="100"> <entry logid="5753304543500710425"> <domain>1</domain> <receive_time>2012/06/13 15:43:17</receive_time> <serial>001606000117</serial> ... <type>TRAFFIC</type> <subtype>start</subtype> ... </entry>  (Note: the live page itself has two typos in this block — a stray extra quote in <response status="success""> and a missing closing quote in progress="100n> — both confirmed present in Palo Alto's own published HTML, not an artifact of this research.)

confirmedFacts.claim: pan-python's log() method does NOT independently corroborate the result/log/logs/entry depth — it stops at confirming job completion (status=='FIN') and returns, leaving entry parsing entirely to the caller via the raw xml_result()/element_root. The CLI tool built on it (panxapi.py --log) likewise just dumps xapi.xml_result() as raw text rather than walking to individual <entry> nodes. So this specific nested xpath rests on the official docs example alone, not on independent SDK-source corroboration.
confirmedFacts.evidence: xapi.log(log_type=options['log'], nlogs=options['nlogs'], ...) is called, then later print(xapi.xml_result()) — no find()/findall() call on 'logs' or 'entry' anywhere in panxapi.py or in xapi.py's log() method.

confirmedFacts.claim: The current, version-agnostic official log-type table (this single consolidated ngfw/api page explicitly covers PAN-OS 11.1, 11.2, 12.1 and 12.2 per its version selector) lists exactly: traffic, threat, config, system, hipmatch, globalprotect, wildfire, url, data, corr, corr-detail, corr-categ, userid, auth, gtp, external, iptag, decryption. There is NO dns or dns-security value in this table.
confirmedFacts.evidence: log-type=traffic —Traffic logs / log-type=threat —Threat logs / log-type=config —Config logs / log-type=system —System logs / log-type=hipmatch / log-type=globalprotect / log-type=wildfire / log-type=url / log-type=data / log-type=corr / log-type=corr-detail / log-type=corr-categ / log-type=userid / log-type=auth / log-type=gtp / log-type=external / log-type=iptag / log-type=decryption

confirmedFacts.claim: A dedicated DNS Security log type is a real PAN-OS product capability, but only from PAN-OS 12.1 onward, and it must be explicitly enabled (Device > Setup > Management > Logging and Reporting Settings > 'Improved DNS Security Logging'). Before that, PAN-OS files DNS Security detections under the Threat log type by category. This directly corroborates the existing pan_api_research.md claim and pins the exact enable path.
confirmedFacts.evidence: "For PAN-OS 12.1 releases and later, DNS Security supports a log type specifically for DNS Security events... This must be specifically enabled by the user, as the previous logs generated for DNS traffic was defined as a DNS threat category, and were subsequently filed under the Threat log type."

confirmedFacts.claim: When PAN-OS 12.1+'s dedicated DNS Security log type IS configured (e.g. in a Log Forwarding Profile's 'Log Type' selector), the literal string used for it is 'dns-security'. This is the strongest concrete lead on what the future XML API log-type= value would likely be (by the established PAN-OS convention that Log Forwarding Profile 'Log Type' names match XML API log-type= values 1:1 for traffic/threat/url/etc), but it is NOT shown in an actual type=log&log-type=dns-security curl/XML example anywhere in official docs — this exact API-parameter usage remains unconfirmed and moot for Suncoast's 11.1/11.2 fleet regardless.
confirmedFacts.evidence: "When selecting the Log Type during the configuration of the log forwarding profile entry, select dns-security."

confirmedFacts.claim: For PAN-OS 11.1/11.2 (Suncoast's actual fleet, pre-12.1), Palo Alto's own official guidance is to query DNS Security activity via the Threat log, not a DNS-specific log type — confirming the existing code's routing decision (get_dns_threat_logs -> log-type=threat) is correct.
confirmedFacts.evidence: "As a result, Palo Alto Networks recommends viewing logs for malicious DNS requests as threat logs instead of DNS Security logs."

confirmedFacts.claim: CONTRADICTS the task's candidate guess: the Threat log's documented 'Subtype' (Threat/Content Type) field does NOT have a 'dns' value. Its full documented enumeration is: data, file, flood, packet, scan, spyware, url, ml-virus, virus, vulnerability, wildfire, wildfire-virus. So a filter of the form 'subtype eq dns' is not a valid/documented way to isolate DNS Security entries in the Threat log — this candidate should be discarded.
confirmedFacts.evidence: "data—Data pattern matching a Data Filtering profile. file—... spyware—Spyware detected via an Anti-Spyware profile. url—URL filtering log. ml-virus—... virus—... vulnerability—... wildfire—... wildfire-virus—..." (dns is absent from this list)

confirmedFacts.claim: The CONFIRMED, officially-documented filter field to isolate DNS Security detections within the Threat log (Monitor > Logs > Threat) is category-of-threatid, with example values dns-c2 and adns-hijacking, and a note that other 'supported DNS category' values exist (ddns, parked, malware, etc. — list explicitly non-exhaustive in the doc). Example filters shown: (category-of-threatid eq dns-c2) and (category-of-threatid eq adns-hijacking).
confirmedFacts.evidence: "Select Monitor > Logs > Threat or DNS Security and filter based on the DNS category. ... (category-of-threatid eq dns-c2) to view logs that have been determined to be a C2 domain by DNS Security. (category-of-threatid eq adns-hijacking), whereby the variable adns-hijacking indicates DNS queries that have been categorized as a malicious DNS hijacking attempt by Advanced DNS Security. To search for other DNS types, replace c2 with another supported DNS category (ddns, parked, malware, etc)."

confirmedFacts.claim: The XML API's type=log 'query' parameter is officially documented as using the SAME filter syntax as the Monitor tab's log-filter GUI ('similar to the query provided in the web interface under the Monitor tab'). This is the direct link that lets the GUI-documented category-of-threatid filter be carried over into the API's query= value (URL-encoded) for a log-type=threat request — e.g. query=(category-of-threatid eq dns-c2). No official page shows this combined with an actual type=log&log-type=threat curl example, so the specific end-to-end combination is inferred from two separate confirmed official statements, not from one single worked example.
confirmedFacts.evidence: "query — (Optional) Specify the match criteria for the logs. This is similar to the query provided in the web interface under the Monitor tab when viewing the logs. The query must be URL encoded."

confirmedFacts.claim: pan-os-python (PaloAltoNetworks/pan-os-python, the official PANW-maintained config-object SDK) has NO log-retrieval-specific method anywhere in its codebase. It only exposes the underlying pan-python XapiWrapper via a .xapi property/op() wrapper; any type=log call would have to be made by dropping down to device.xapi.log(...) from pan-python directly. This is a useful negative finding: pan-os-python is not a corroborating source for log-retrieval shape at all.
confirmedFacts.evidence: grep of panos/base.py (master branch) for 'def.*log|log-type|job-id' returns nothing except the unrelated .xapi property (line 4103) and op() method (line 4108) — no log()/get_logs() method exists in the class hierarchy.

confirmedFacts.claim: pan.dev (Palo Alto's developer portal) has NO PAN-OS XML/REST API reference for log retrieval at all — that content lives exclusively on docs.paloaltonetworks.com. pan.dev does host a distinct '/dns-security/api/' page, but it is a BETA cloud domain-reputation lookup RESTful API (separate product), unrelated to firewall log retrieval, PAN-OS log-type values, or the XML API job/poll mechanic. Do not conflate the two.
confirmedFacts.evidence: "access information about domains processed by DNS Security through a programmatic RESTful API" — a per-organization API key, currently BETA, requires an active DNS Security subscription; no mention of PAN-OS, XML API, Panorama, or log-type anywhere on the page.

remainingGaps: No live device to confirm the raw pending-job response body verbatim — official docs only state in prose that <log> is absent while pending; no worked XML example of the intermediate/pending poll response exists anywhere found (not on docs.paloaltonetworks.com, not in pan-python source comments). The exact contents of result/job/status while pending (e.g. literal text 'ACT' vs 'PEND' vs something else) is inferred only from tangential PAN-OS job-status terminology (commit/show-jobs KB articles), not from a type=log-specific example.

Whether a completed job with zero matching entries still emits an empty <logs count="0"></logs> node (so result/log/logs/entry findall() safely returns []) or omits <logs> entirely is not shown in any official example — current _parse_log_entries's empty-list fallback is a reasonable assumption but unverified.

Whether the category-of-threatid filter (or any query= filter at all) actually works when combined with type=log&log-type=threat via the raw XML API — every confirmed example of category-of-threatid comes from the Monitor > Logs GUI filter builder page, and every confirmed example of query= URL-encoding comes from a generic traffic-log (receive_time) example. No single official page shows both combined in one curl example.

The complete, non-'etc'-truncated list of DNS category values valid for category-of-threatid on a base (non-Advanced) DNS Security subscription on PAN-OS 11.1.13/11.2.10-H3 specifically — docs only give dns-c2, adns-hijacking, ddns, parked, malware as examples and explicitly say '(etc)', leaving the full enumeration unconfirmed.

Whether target=<serial> (Panorama-proxying) works with type=log at all — still completely unaddressed by any official page found in this pass (unchanged from the prior research file's gap #6); this blocks knowing whether get_dns_threat_logs/get_traffic_logs can be called against Panorama's own hostname with target= for a managed firewall, or must be called directly against each firewall.

The exact literal XML API log-type= string for PAN-OS 12.1+'s dedicated DNS Security log type is inferred (dns-security) from a Log Forwarding Profile config-UI screen, not confirmed from an actual type=log&log-type=dns-security curl/XML example — moot for Suncoast's current 11.1/11.2 fleet but would need live confirmation before any future upgrade-driven code change.

No LIVEcommunity/forum thread was found that specifically discusses querying DNS Security or DNS sinkhole logs through the type=log XML API (as opposed to the GUI) — the one thread fetched (382366) returned an access error (403) and could not be read; this leaves zero community-forum corroboration in this research pass, despite it being one of the requested source tiers.

recommendedCodeChanges.change: In _xml_log_poll, the completion check root.find('./result/log') is None is a reasonable heuristic that matches the docs' prose statement, but it's weaker than the reference SDK's mechanic. Recommend also reading root.find('./result/job/status') and checking .text == 'FIN' (as pan-python's xapi.py log() method does at github.com/kevinsteves/pan-python/blob/master/lib/pan/xapi.py lines 1154-1159), and raising PanXmlApiError with the actual status text if it's present but not FIN and not a recognized in-progress value after max_wait_seconds — this gives a diagnosable error instead of a bare TimeoutError when a job fails/errors out rather than merely running long.

get_dns_threat_logs's docstring currently flags the filter field as an unconfirmed open gap. Update it: the confirmed field is category-of-threatid (not 'subtype', which is confirmed NOT to carry a dns value per docs.paloaltonetworks.com/ngfw/administration/monitoring/use-syslog-for-monitoring/syslog-field-descriptions/threat-log-fields). Example confirmed-syntax filters to suggest as defaults/documentation: query='(category-of-threatid eq dns-c2)' or '(category-of-threatid eq adns-hijacking)', sourced from docs.paloaltonetworks.com/dns-security/administration/monitor-dns-security/view-dns-security-logs. Still flag as an open gap that the full DNS-category value list is non-exhaustive in official docs and that combining category-of-threatid with type=log&log-type=threat via the raw API (as opposed to the GUI) has no official worked example — needs live-device confirmation before treating as production-ready.

Update section 5 ('Traffic / URL Filtering / DNS Security Logs'): replace 'Open gap: the exact filter value/category name... is not confirmed' with the now-confirmed category-of-threatid field and example values (dns-c2, adns-hijacking, ddns, parked, malware), citing docs.paloaltonetworks.com/dns-security/administration/monitor-dns-security/view-dns-security-logs. Also add a forward-looking note that PAN-OS 12.1+ introduces a dedicated log type (GUI/Log-Forwarding-Profile string 'dns-security', per docs.paloaltonetworks.com/dns-security/administration/monitor-dns-security/enable-dns-security-log-type) that Suncoast should adopt if/when their fleet is upgraded past 11.2, since it would eliminate the threat-log-filtering workaround entirely.
